title: I built a non-LLM quant investment platform that scores its own predictions every trading day
author: MehmetSaruhan

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: Comparing its own past forecasts every day is good, most platforms never show the misses. I'd put a dumb baseline right next to it, like last month's return carried forward, so a reader can tell skill apart from a tape that just trended.

replies.author: MehmetSaruhan
replies.body: As you know, the direction accuracy rate and IC value of a good machine learning model are around 55% and 0.03, respectively; no model can make predictions with 100% accuracy. What really matters is how you can reduce this risk! We offer 5 different intelligence(Agentic) services to help ensure a book turns a profit one month from now... You can try it for free for 30 days, no CC.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: an IC of 0.03 is honest, and it's also small enough for trading costs to eat. I'd want the daily scores shown net of costs before any monthly profit claim.

replies.author: MehmetSaruhan
replies.body: We use the **Almgren-Chriss** cost model and published FINRA daily cost etc. So all costs are computed by the platform. When I meant the 1 month, we have the swing trading approach not intraday trading. So a book needs rebalance and triggered by stop params couple of time to beat the S&P statistically.

comments.author: Mysterious_Water6337
comments.body: The daily self scoring part is probably the strongest idea here. Plenty of quant tools show forecasts but make it weirdly difficult to see how yesterday’s forecasts actually aged. I would add a brutally simple benchmark next to every model so users can tell real signal from a friendly market regime. Moon is almost the opposite use case, useful for expressing a directional view rather than running an adaptive investment portfolio.

replies.author: MehmetSaruhan
replies.body:
We have 10 model families and nearly 100 ML models, combined through our BOA engine. BOA continuously evaluates how each model’s past predictions actually performed and dynamically adjusts their contribution to the next ensemble prediction. This has brought the aggregate directional accuracy to around 58.2%.

But our R&D over the last three years led us to a more important conclusion: **predictions alone are not sufficient for trading.** You cannot realistically expect 90% statistical confidence from individual market predictions, so simply presenting a forecast and asking the user to trade on it is not the approach we built.

Instead, we developed an agentic investment process around the predictions, with around 80 configurable portfolio and strategy parameters covering things such as risk, position sizing, exits, holding periods and portfolio construction.

So when a user signs in, they don't need to interpret dozens of model outputs. They select one of three portfolio presets based on their risk profile, and the system runs the portfolio process accordingly.

In other words, the prediction is **evidence entering the decision process—not the decision itself.**

comments.author: tradematesHQ
comments.body: The daily self scoring is the only part of this that matters. Anyone can bolt gradient boosted trees onto price data, but showing how yesterday's calls actually aged is rare. The catch is that a scoring loop flatters itself if it grades gross of costs, so the number that counts is the one net of slippage and fees. Put a dumb baseline right next to every model, like last month's return carried forward, so a reader can tell skill from a tape that just trended. Without that, the accuracy figure is just a friendly market regime wearing a lab coat. Worth cross-checking the scoring methodology against independent analysis on sites like trademates or similar before trusting the loop.

replies.author: MehmetSaruhan
replies.body:
[https://www.reddit.com/r/ai\_trading/comments/1wpc8ni/comment/pbx806i/?utm\_source=share&utm\_medium=web3x&utm\_name=web3xcss&utm\_term=1&utm\_content=share\_button](https://www.reddit.com/r/ai_trading/comments/1wpc8ni/comment/pbx806i/?utm_source=share&utm_medium=web3x&utm_name=web3xcss&utm_term=1&utm_content=share_button)

I answered in this comment. Furthermore, gradient boosted models can't reach 58.2 dir. acc. with price history! However: "What representation is rich enough to describe a security's condition across independent domains, without collapsing into redundant restatements of price?

Every security, every trading day, is represented as a 1,979-dimensional state vector constructed across orthogonal domains: price kinematics, order-flow and microstructure behaviour; multi-horizon trend persistence; graph-neural-network (GNN) representations of cross-asset and corporate relationship structure; corporate and cross-asset sentiment parsed with domain-specific NLP — FinBERT and the Loughran-McDonald financial dictionaries — rather than general-purpose scoring, which systematically misreads financial language; multi-scale Daubechies-4 wavelet decomposition and geometric pattern structure; period-matched fundamentals from filings; explicit Fama-French factor-exposure decomposition; macro-financial regime conditioning; and intrinsic-value dislocation measures.

Volatility structure is modelled with higher-order estimators — realised semivariance, bipower jump share, realised skew and kurtosis — rather than a single dispersion measure. Unsupervised anomaly detection (Isolation Forest) flags statistically unusual states that no supervised label anticipates. The macro layer contributes 530+ engineered multi-horizon indicators."
